transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-30 15:00 UTC | Duration 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (RE), Jordan Lee (CISO - Lumina), Maya Patel (Cloud Ops), Tom Alvarez (DevOps), Rina Cho (Compliance)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. This is Alex from Redwood, joined by Priya and Samir on the technical side. Jordan, thanks for pulling the team together.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Yeah thanks Alex, wanted to go through audit logs and admin activity — specifically what you capture, how we can export, retention, and keys. We have auditors next quarter so want to be explicit.
[00:32] Priya Nair: Great, we'll run through the event types first then export and retention. Quick note: transcript may have a few mislabeled words, sorry in advance.
[00:45] Samir Gupta: Starting with events: we capture admin auth events (SSO/SAML logins, MFA failures), API key create/rotate/revoke, role and permission changes, user invites/removals, changes to model routing and rollout configs, Dedicated instance lifecycle events, and important system-level alerts e.g., failed backups or audit export errors.
[01:10] Tom Alvarez: Do you also capture token issuance details — like which token was issued for which service?
[01:18] Priya Nair: Yes, we log token issuance and token revocations with the issuer principal, IP, timestamp, and if available the SAML assertion subject. We don't store raw tokens in logs; just the meta.
[01:32] Maya Patel: Good. For compliance we need immutability and tamper evidence — is the audit log append-only and can Lumina use its own cloud storage?
[01:44] Alex Chen: Right now we provide multiple sinks: S3 (recommended for most customers), syslog (for on-prem SIEM), Kafka, and direct API pulls for SIEMs. S3 exports can be set to use object lock (WORM) on the bucket side — if you enable bucket-level immutability it satisfies the append-only requirement.
[02:08] Jordan Lee: Does Redwood support customer-managed keys for S3 exports/encryption at rest? We need CMKs/HSM integration for keys.
[02:17] Priya Nair: For data at rest inside Redwood, we use envelope encryption. You can opt for customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) via KMS — both AWS KMS and external HSM integrations are supported for Private deployments. For hosted customers we support using a CMK in your account when using S3 export; if you need a true HSM-backed key we can discuss Private deployment options.
[02:42] Rina Cho: Are admin actions correlated to user identity? We have cases where tooling calls internal service accounts — we need to distinguish humans vs service principals.
[02:52] Samir Gupta: We log the authenticated principal as presented by the auth layer — SAML subject or OIDC sub — and include attributes like principal type when available. Service accounts will appear with a service account identifier. We also capture IP, user agent, and session duration for login events.
[03:12] Tom Alvarez: How frequent are exports? Can we stream in near real-time?
[03:18] Priya Nair: Yes, we have two modes: batched export (e.g., hourly/daily files to S3) and streaming (syslog/Kafka) which is near real-time. Streaming has small batching for efficiency but it's effectively realtime for SIEM use cases.
[03:32] Jordan Lee: We use Splunk/Enterprise Security — any pre-built connectors?
[03:36] Alex Chen: No out-of-the-box Splunk app yet, but customers use either the syslog sink or S3 with a Splunk ingestion job. We can share a sample HEC/Splunk ingest config and a sample log schema to make mapping simpler.
[03:52] Maya Patel: What format are the logs in? JSON? Fields? Can you share sample events?
[03:58] Priya Nair: Primary format is JSON lines with a documented schema. Top-level fields include timestamp (ISO-8601), event_type, actor/principal, principal_type, ip_address, user_agent, target (resource affected), action, outcome (success/failure), request_id, and an optional metadata blob. We'll send a sample schema.
[04:22] Samir Gupta: Quick aside — sometimes the transcript will show KV cash instead of KV cache, just FYI.
[04:30] (laughter)
[04:34] Jordan Lee: About retention — what are defaults and what can we configure? Our policy is 1 year for admin logs but auditors ask for 7 years in some cases.
[04:44] Alex Chen: Hosted default retention is 90 days for audit logs but you can request extended retention—common tiers are 90, 365, and custom (archival to S3 for long-term). For Dedicated and Private deployments you control retention entirely — we can export logs to your S3 with lifecycle rules to meet 7-year retention.
[05:06] Rina Cho: Any support for legal hold / eDiscovery?
[05:10] Priya Nair: We have a legal-hold flow for Dedicated/Private where you can mark specific objects or date ranges as on hold; for hosted customers we can set up an export and keep a retained copy in your account. We'll need legal approval for longer holds on hosted accounts.
[05:28] Tom Alvarez: How are sensitive fields handled? Are there PII redaction options?
[05:34] Samir Gupta: We don't log full request payloads by default. For anything that could include PII we recommend filtering on the client side before sending, and we can support redaction rules in the export pipeline — e.g., mask username/email in logs. We'll share options in the schema doc.
[05:52] Jordan Lee: What about RBAC/SSO — do audit logs capture role assignment changes and policy changes from SCIM?
[05:58] Priya Nair: Yes, role assignment changes, SCIM provisioning events, group sync, and SAML assertion failures are logged. Each event includes the before/after where possible. There are also audit events for admin UI actions (console changes) and API-driven changes.
[06:18] Maya Patel: For SIEM correlation we need a stable request_id across services. Does Redwood surface a request_id that we can join to other telemetry?
[06:26] Alex Chen: We include request_id, and for multi-service flows we try to surface a trace id when available — it's best-effort but we do emit correlation ids for API requests. We'll include guidance on how to surface these in your logging.
[06:44] Jordan Lee: In terms of alerting, can Redwood push admin-failure alerts or suspicious activity to our PagerDuty / SNS?
[06:52] Priya Nair: We have alerting hooks: webhook, PagerDuty, and integrations via SIEM. For hosted customers we provide an alerts API to subscribe to specific event types; Dedicated/private customers can run our alerting connectors locally.
[07:06] Tom Alvarez: Performance — if we enable streaming of high-volume events to Kafka, any throughput limits? We run at scale.
[07:14] Samir Gupta: For streaming sinks we rate limit per-account but limits are high; for very heavy customers we recommend Dedicated or a dedicated streaming endpoint — we can raise the throughput during the POC. We'll surface typical throughput numbers in the doc.
[07:32] Jordan Lee: One more on encryption — is server-side encryption with customer keys supported for objects you store? And do you rotate keys regularly?
[07:40] Priya Nair: For S3 exports using your bucket, encryption is controlled by your bucket settings and your KMS. Inside Redwood, we rotate envelope keys regularly; if you bring your own CMK we do not rotate that key (that's on you) but we rotate the data keys. For Private deployments we can support HSM-backed keys and auditable key usage logs.
[07:58] Rina Cho: Can we get the SOC2 report and ISO attestation?
[08:02] Alex Chen: Absolutely — we'll attach our latest SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation in the follow-up email.
[08:10] Jordan Lee: Great. Next steps?
[08:14] Alex Chen: Recap: we'll send the security whitepaper and certificates, sample audit log schema, and an S3/syslog export runbook. Priya will set up a test sink for the POC and share instructions. Lumina will confirm retention window and legal hold requirements.
[08:30] Maya Patel: We'll aim for 365 as the baseline and flag any items needing 7 years.
[08:36] Tom Alvarez: For the POC, can you populate a sample stream with historic admin events?
[08:41] Priya Nair: Yes we can replay anonymized historic events to your test sink — we'll do that for the POC.
[08:48] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[08:52] Alex Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription shows timestamps roughly every 15-90s; minor transcription errors expected. References: security whitepaper (link), SOC2 report (link), sample log schema (will be attached in follow-up).
